messages:
jasper: Quick heads-up — seeing weird tail on all-reduce during 8-GPU inference run. p95 jumps ~18% mid-run. can we probe NCCL algo/proto/channel combos?

marta: what workload? batch size, seq len, kv cache hit rate?

jasper: 8xA100, TP=2, PP=4, seq=2048, micro-batch=1, KV cache enabled (avg prefix 512), steady QPS ~220. repro around step 1200 after some cache churn.

chen: ok. first hypothesis: channel contention + small collectives during KV updates. try: NCCL_ALGO=TREE / RING, NCCL_PROTO=LL / LL128, NCCL_MAX_RINGS=1/2? also test NCCL_NSOCKS_PER_THREAD tweaks.

oliver: also collect nsys traces around the spike. we need comm/compute overlap breakdown. can you run the following quick probes?

jasper: yeah running now. sharing snippets when done.

perf-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1765438910/trace.zip (contains nsys, nvprof, nccl-tests outputs) :package:

marta: saw the artifact. quick glance: all-reduce tail grows from 2.4ms -> 4.1ms at the spike. bandwidth steady. implies serialization/queueing, not raw link saturation.

jasper: here's a short paste of microbench (nccl-tests all_reduce -b 256k -e 256k -f 2 -g 8):

```
# nccl-tests all_reduce sample
bytes    #ops   avg(us)   min(us)   max(us)
262144   128    2400      2200      4120
```

chen: try LL vs LL128 numbers? ll128 tends to reduce latency jitter for small messages on A100.

jasper: ran LL and LL128:

```
# NCCL_PROTO=LL
avg 2350us, p99 4100us
# NCCL_PROTO=LL128
avg 2200us, p99 2900us
```

marta: LL128 helped but p99 still high under KV churn. what's the KV update pattern? many small all-reduces?

jasper: KV updates happen every token for cache misses — lots of tiny collectives (~8-32KB).

oliver: tiny collectives are the killer. enable small-message optimizations: NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=131072(?) and NCCL_ALGO=RING for tiny sizes. also test channel count: NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME vs NCCL_NTHREADS?

chen: we should sample with varying channel counts: NCCL_NCHANNELS=1,2,4. channels increase concurrency but can worsen ordering for tiny ops. run a 30-min sweep with synthetic KV churn (simulate 10% miss).

jasper: starting sweep: configs queued: [LL128+NCHANNELS=1, LL128+NCHANNELS=4, LL+NCHANNELS=1, LL+NCHANNELS=4, PROTO=SIMPLE+RING] — will post results.

marta: also instrument kernel selection hotpath in runtime: log selected kernel id + seq length for those requests. want to see if wrong kernel chosen after cache churn.

jasper: good point. adding logging. quick sample results (averaged across 10 mins):

```
config                              avg_token_ms   p99_token_ms
LL128 + NCHANNELS=1                  11.4           19.8
LL128 + NCHANNELS=4                  10.9           28.3
LL + NCHANNELS=1                     12.8           36.5
SIMPLE + RING                        13.6           31.1
```

chen: interesting: NCHANNELS=4 lowers avg but increases tail. matches hypothesis: parallel channels reduce avg latency but increase jitter due to ordering/skew.

oliver: action items: (1) enable LL128 by default for A100 inference workloads with heavy KV churn, (2) fall back to NCHANNELS=1 for strict p99 SLAs, (3) add runtime heuristic: pick NCHANNELS based on observed small-op fraction and recent p99.

marta: for kernel selection: if prefix length > 256 and kv-hit-rate < 0.9, prefer low-latency kernel variant even if lower throughput. add counter for kernel mispredictions.

jasper: created perf ticket: INF-1278 with sample traces + nccl sweep csv. tagging @oliver @chen for review.

perf-bot: perf ticket INF-1278 created by jasper — link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-1278 :memo:

chen: i'll take point on adding the runtime heuristic and scoring function for channel selection. will prototype a simple rule first, then ML-ish scorer later.

marta: i'll prep a canary config for dedicated clusters: LL128 default + NCHANNELS=1 policy toggle. we should run a week of canary to measure tail improvements.

jasper: thanks all — will follow up with the full sweep CSV and traces in the ticket. :thumbsup:
